questions.text: क्रोमेटीन के अपने विस्तारित रूप 'डोरी पर बीड्स' सदृश संरचना में 'बीड्स' इनसे बने होते हैं :
questions.text_english: In its extended 'beads-on-string' form of chromatin, the 'beads' are composed of :

options.B: हिस्टोन तथा लगभग 200 bp वाले डीएनए
options.D: एनएचसी प्रोटीन तथा लगभग 200 bp वाले डीएनए

options_english.B: Histones and about 200 bp of DNA
options_english.D: NHC proteins and about 200 bp of DNA

questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. Each nucleosome, which appears as a 'bead' in the beads-on-string model, consists of a histone octamer (two copies each of H2A, H2B, H3 and H4) around which about 200 bp of DNA is wrapped. Option (A) is wrong because linker DNA connects nucleosomes but is not part of the bead itself. Options (C) and (D) are wrong because NHC (Non-Histone Chromosomal) proteins are not components of the nucleosome bead.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (B) सही है। प्रत्येक न्यूक्लियोसोम 'बीड' हिस्टोन ऑक्टामर से बना होता है जिसके चारों ओर लगभग 200 bp डीएनए लिपटा होता है।

questions.text: मानव अंडाशय में अंडजनन (ऊजेनेसिस) प्रक्रम के संबंध में कुछ कथन नीचे दिए गए हैं : (i) प्राथमिक पुटक का निर्माण करने हेतु कणिकामय कोशिकाओं (ग्रेनुलोसा सेल्स) की प्रत्येक कोशिका प्राथमिक अंडक कोशिका द्वारा आवृत हो जाती है। (ii) भ्रूणीय परिवर्धन के दौरान प्रत्येक भ्रूणीय अंडाशय के अंदर कई मिलियन अंडजननी (ऊगोनिया) विनिर्मित होती हैं। (iii) एक गह्वर (एंट्रूम) तथा प्रावरक स्तर (थीका लेयर) तृतीयक पुटक के अभिलाक्षणिक गुण हैं। (iv) द्वितीयक पुटक अपने चारों ओर एक पारदर्शी अंडावरण (जोना पेल्यूसिडा) परत का निर्माण करता है। (v) परिपक्व ग्राफी पुटक अंडाशय से द्वितीयक अंडक को मोचित करने हेतु फट जाता है। दिए गए विकल्पों से उस विकल्प को चुनिए जिसके सभी कथन सत्य हैं :
questions.text_english: Given below are few statements with respect to the process of oogenesis in a human ovary : (i) Each granulosa cell gets surrounded by a primary oocyte to form the primary follicle. (ii) A couple of million of oogonia are formed within each fetal ovary during the embryonic development. (iii) Tertiary follicle is characterised by antrum and theca layers. (iv) Secondary follicles form a zona pellucida layer around it. (v) Mature graafian follicle ruptures to release the secondary oocyte from the ovary. Choose the option with all true statements from the given options :
questions.instruction_line: दिए गए विकल्पों से उस विकल्प को चुनिए जिसके सभी कथन सत्य हैं।
questions.instruction_line_english: Choose the option with all true statements from the given options.
questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. Statement (ii) is true — millions of oogonia are formed in the fetal ovary. Statement (iii) is true — the tertiary follicle is characterised by a fluid-filled antrum and theca layer. Statement (v) is true — the mature Graafian follicle ruptures to release the secondary oocyte. Statement (i) is false because it is the primary oocyte that is surrounded by granulosa cells, not the other way around. Statement (iv) is false because zona pellucida forms around the secondary follicle, not the primary follicle.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (B) सही है। कथन (ii), (iii) और (v) सत्य हैं।

questions.text: सुकेंद्रकी में जीन की सरलतम परिभाषा है – डीएनए की वह इकाई जिसमें इसके संश्लेषण की विशिष्ट सूचना निहित होती है :
questions.text_english: The simplest definition of a gene in eukaryotes is – A unit of DNA that has information to mainly specify the synthesis of :

options.A: एकल पॉलीपेप्टाइड श्रृंखला तथा केवल एमआरएनए
options.B: अनेक पॉलीपेप्टाइड श्रृंखलाएँ तथा केवल एमआरएनए
options.C: एकल पॉलीपेप्टाइड श्रृंखला तथा केवल क्रियाशील आरएनए
options.D: अनेक पॉलीपेप्टाइड श्रृंखलाएँ तथा केवल क्रियाशील आरएनए

options_english.A: Single polypeptide chain and mRNA only
options_english.B: Many polypeptide chains and mRNA only
options_english.C: Single polypeptide chain and functional RNA only
options_english.D: Many polypeptide chains and functional RNA only

questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. The simplest definition of a gene in eukaryotes is a segment of DNA that encodes information for either a single polypeptide chain or a functional RNA (such as rRNA or tRNA). A single gene encodes a single polypeptide; if multiple polypeptides are needed, multiple genes are involved. Option (A) is wrong because genes can specify functional RNA, not just mRNA. Options (B) and (D) are wrong because one gene specifies one polypeptide, not many.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) सही है। सुकेंद्रकी में एक जीन एकल पॉलीपेप्टाइड श्रृंखला या क्रियाशील आरएनए के संश्लेषण की सूचना रखता है।

questions.text: एक वर्णांध पुरुष ने एक सामान्य दृष्टि की स्त्री के साथ विवाह किया जिसके परिवार में वर्णांधता विकार का कोई इतिहास नहीं है। उस युगल (दंपति) के पुत्र के वर्णांध होने की संभावता कितनी है ?
questions.text_english: A colourblind man marries a woman with normal sight who has no history of colourblindness in her family. What is the probability of their son being colourblind ?
questions.solution: Option (C) — Nil — is correct. Colour blindness is an X-linked recessive trait. The colourblind father has genotype X^c Y and the normal-sighted mother, with no family history, has genotype X^N X^N. Their sons will receive Y from father and X^N from mother, giving X^N Y — all sons will have normal vision. Therefore, the probability of their son being colourblind is zero. Option (A) and (B) would apply only if the mother were a carrier.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) शून्य सही है। वर्णांधता X-सहलग्न अप्रभावी लक्षण है। पिता X^c Y और माता X^N X^N होने से सभी पुत्र X^N Y होंगे, अर्थात सामान्य।

questions.text: किसी व्यक्ति में धूल तथा परागकणों जैसे कुछ प्रतिजनों के प्रति प्रतिरक्षित अनुक्रिया हेतु बनने वाला प्रतिरक्षी है :
questions.text_english: The type of antibodies produced during an immune response to allergens as dust and pollen grains in a person is :
questions.solution: Option (A) IgE is correct. IgE antibodies are specifically produced in allergic reactions triggered by allergens such as dust, pollen, and certain food substances. IgE binds to mast cells and basophils, causing release of histamine and other mediators responsible for allergic symptoms. IgA is found in secretions, IgG provides long-term immunity, and IgD functions as a B-cell receptor — none of these mediate allergic responses.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (A) IgE सही है। एलर्जिक अनुक्रिया में IgE प्रतिरक्षी बनता है जो मास्ट कोशिकाओं से हिस्टामिन मुक्त कराता है।

questions.text: उन कथनों को चुनिए जो पुष्पी पादपों की प्रारूपिक गुरुबीजाणुधानी के लिए सत्य हैं। (i) यह बीजांडवृंत द्वारा अपरा से जुड़ी होती है। (ii) इसका निभाग (कैलाजा) सिरा बीजाण्ड के आधारी भाग का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है। (iii) इसमें अध्यावरणी द्वारा आवृत बीजाण्डकाय होता है। (iv) इसके बीजाण्डद्वारी सिरे को निभाग (कैलाजा) कहते हैं। सही उत्तर चुनिए :
questions.text_english: Select the statements that are true for a typical megasporangium of flowering plants. (i) It is attached to the placenta by hilum. (ii) It has a chalaza end that represents the basal part of the ovule. (iii) It has nucellus enclosed by integuments. (iv) Its micropylar end is known as chalaza. Choose the correct answer :
questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. Statement (ii) is true — the chalaza represents the basal part of the ovule where the nucellus and integuments are fused. Statement (iii) is true — the ovule (megasporangium) contains the nucellus which is surrounded by integuments. Statement (i) is false because the ovule is attached to the placenta by the funicle (funiculus), not the hilum; the hilum is the point of attachment. Statement (iv) is false because the micropylar end is the end with the micropyle opening, whereas chalaza is the opposite basal end.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (B) सही है। कथन (ii) और (iii) सत्य हैं। बीजाण्ड बीजांडवृंत द्वारा अपरा से जुड़ा होता है और इसमें अध्यावरण से घिरा बीजाण्डकाय होता है।

questions.text: लगभग 2 मिलियन वर्ष पूर्व संभवतः पूर्वी अफ्रीका के घास स्थलों में रहने (पाए जाने) वाले प्राइमेट्स थे :
questions.text_english: The primates that probably lived in East Africa grasslands about two mya were :
questions.solution: Option (C) Australopithecines is correct. Australopithecines lived in East African grasslands approximately 2 million years ago (2 mya). They were bipedal and are considered the first hominids. Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus lived much earlier (about 15 mya), while Neanderthals appeared much later, around 1,00,000 years ago in Europe and parts of Asia.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) ऑस्ट्रालोपिथेसिन सही है। ये लगभग 2 मिलियन वर्ष पूर्व पूर्वी अफ्रीका के घास के मैदानों में रहते थे।

questions.text: यदि अनुलेखित किए जाने वाले संरचनात्मक जीन की कोडिंग रज्जुक का न्यूक्लियोटाइड अनुक्रम 'ATA' है, तो स्थानांतरण प्रक्रिया के दौरान टीआरएनए (tRNA) के 3' सिरे से जुड़े हुए ऐमीनो अम्ल को दी गई सूचना का उपयोग करके चुनिए।
questions.text_english: Use the given information to select the amino acid attached to the 3' end of tRNA during the process of translation, if the coding strand of the structural gene being transcribed has the nucleotide sequence 'ATA'. Codons for the amino acids: UAU – Tyrosine, AUG – Methionine, AUA – Isoleucine, AGU – Serine.
questions.instruction_line: दी गई सूचना का उपयोग करके चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Use the given information to select the correct option.
questions.solution: Option (C) Tyrosine is correct. The coding strand sequence is 3'-ATA-5' (written in 5'→3' direction as ATA, but the template strand used for transcription is the complementary strand). The coding strand ATA (5'→3') corresponds to template strand TAT (3'→5'), which gives mRNA codon UAU. According to the given table, UAU codes for Tyrosine. The tRNA anticodon will be AUA, and the amino acid attached to the 3' end of the tRNA will be Tyrosine.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) टाइरोसीन सही है। कोडिंग स्ट्रैंड ATA से टेम्पलेट स्ट्रैंड TAT बनता है, जिससे mRNA कोडॉन UAU बनता है जो टाइरोसीन को कोड करता है।

questions.text: एड्स के संदिग्ध रोगियों में एचआईवी की प्रारंभिक अवस्था में पहचान हेतु नैदानिक तकनीक का नाम है :
questions.text_english: Early detection of HIV in suspected AIDS patients can be done using the diagnostic technique of :
questions.solution: Option (B) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) is correct. PCR can detect HIV even in the early stages of infection when the viral load is very low and antibodies have not yet been produced. It amplifies the viral RNA/DNA to detectable levels. ELISA detects antibodies against HIV, which appear only after a window period. EST (Expressed Sequence Tags) is used in gene discovery. RNAi is a gene-silencing technique, not a diagnostic method.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (B) PCR सही है। PCR तकनीक से HIV के संक्रमण की प्रारंभिक अवस्था में ही वायरल RNA का पता लगाया जा सकता है।

questions.text: यह सिद्ध करने के लिए कि डीएनए अर्धसंरक्षी प्रतिकृतियन करता है, मैथ्यू मेसेल्सन एवं फ्रैंकलिन स्टाल द्वारा किए गए प्रयोग में अपकेन्द्रण द्वारा 40 मिनट बाद संवर्धन से निष्कर्षित किए गए डीएनए को ठीक (सही) प्रकार से प्रदर्शित करने वाला आरेख है :
questions.text_english: The correct depiction of the experiment performed by Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl to prove that DNA replicates semi-conservatively on separation of DNA by centrifugation after 40 minutes is :

options.A: Two dark bands in the middle
options.B: One band at bottom (heavy) and one band in middle (hybrid)
options.C: One dark band and one light-dark hybrid band
options.D: Only one band at the bottom

options_english.A: Two dark bands in the middle (hybrid)
options_english.B: One heavy band at bottom and one hybrid band in middle
options_english.C: One dark band at one position and one hybrid band
options_english.D: Only one band at the bottom (heavy)

questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. In the Meselson-Stahl experiment, bacteria were first grown in 15N (heavy nitrogen) medium so all DNA was heavy (15N-15N). After 40 minutes (one generation) in 14N medium, each DNA molecule replicated once, producing two hybrid DNA molecules (15N-14N). On CsCl density gradient centrifugation, these appear as a single band at an intermediate position between pure heavy and pure light DNA. Therefore, after 40 minutes, there should be one hybrid band in the middle, confirming semi-conservative replication.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (B) सही है। 40 मिनट बाद (एक पीढ़ी) सभी DNA अणु 15N-14N संकर होंगे और CsCl अपकेन्द्रण पर एक मध्यवर्ती बैंड दिखाएंगे।

questions.text: 'स्विस चीज़' में पाए जाने वाले बड़े-बड़े छिद्र जिन सूक्ष्मजीवों की क्रिया के कारण बनते हैं, वह है :
questions.text_english: Large holes in 'Swiss cheese' are formed by the activity of microbes :
questions.solution: Option (D) Propionibacterium sharmanii is correct. The large holes characteristic of Swiss cheese are produced by carbon dioxide gas generated by Propionibacterium sharmanii during fermentation. Streptococcus pneumoniae is a disease-causing bacterium. Monascus purpureus is used to make statins (lovastatin). Trichoderma polysporum is the source of cyclosporin A (an immunosuppressant drug).
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (D) Propionibacterium sharmanii सही है। यह CO2 गैस उत्पन्न करता है जिससे स्विस चीज़ में बड़े-बड़े छिद्र बनते हैं।

questions.text: मटर के पौधे (पाइसम सैटाइवम) में पुष्प की अक्षीय स्थिति, पुष्पों की अंत्य स्थिति पर प्रभावी है। एक क्रॉस जिसमें दोनों जनक विषमयुग्मजी अक्षीय पुष्प हैं, की संतति के दृश्यरूप (फीनोटाइप) का अनुमानित अनुपात होगा :
questions.text_english: In pea plant (Pisum sativum) axial flower position is dominant over terminal flower position. The expected ratio of phenotypes of the offspring in a cross between both the parents with heterozygous axial flower will be :
questions.solution: Option (A) 3 : 1 is correct. When two heterozygous axial plants (Aa × Aa) are crossed, the offspring ratio is 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa. Since axial (A) is dominant over terminal (a), both AA and Aa show axial phenotype, while aa shows terminal phenotype. This gives a phenotypic ratio of 3 axial : 1 terminal, which is the classic Mendelian monohybrid ratio.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (A) 3 : 1 सही है। Aa × Aa क्रॉस में 3 अक्षीय (AA + Aa) : 1 अंत्य (aa) का फीनोटाइप अनुपात मिलता है।

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : मुँह से खाई जाने वाली 'सहेली' नामक गर्भनिरोधक गोली अंडोत्सर्जन को संदमित करती है तथा शुक्राणुओं की भक्षकाणुक्रिया (फेगोसाइटोसिस) बढ़ा देती है। कारण (R) : यह एक गैर-स्टेरॉइडली सामग्री है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : 'Saheli', an oral contraceptive inhibits ovulation and increases phagocytosis of sperms. Reason (R) : It is a non-steroidal preparation.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) के लिए सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer for Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. The Assertion is true — Saheli (centchroman) is an oral contraceptive that inhibits ovulation and increases phagocytosis of sperms. The Reason is also true — Saheli is indeed a non-steroidal preparation, making it distinct from hormonal oral contraceptives. However, the Reason does not explain why Saheli inhibits ovulation or increases phagocytosis. The non-steroidal nature is a chemical property, not the mechanism of its contraceptive action. Hence both statements are true but R does not correctly explain A.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (B) सही है। दोनों कथन सत्य हैं, परंतु कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : संक्रमित पौधों से विषाणु-मुक्त (वायरस रहित) पौधे प्राप्त करने के लिए उनके विभज्योतकों का 'पात्रे' संवर्धन किया जाता है। कारण (R) : यदि पौधा विषाणु से संक्रमित होता है, तो उसकी जड़ें तथा स्तम्भ (तना) विषाणु मुक्त रहते हैं।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : The meristems are grown 'in vitro' to obtain virus-free plants from an infected plant. Reason (R) : If the plant is infected with a virus, the roots and the stems are free of virus.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true, but R is false.
options.D: A is false, but R is true.

options_english.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options_english.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options_english.C: A is true, but R is false.

sub_questions.solution: When the same restriction enzyme EcoR I is used to cut both the vector DNA and the alien (insert) DNA, it generates identical complementary sticky ends (single-stranded overhangs) on both DNA fragments. These compatible sticky ends can then anneal (base-pair) with each other through hydrogen bonding. This makes it possible for DNA Ligase to join them covalently, forming a stable recombinant DNA molecule. If different restriction enzymes were used, incompatible ends would be produced and ligation would not occur.

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain how the interaction between sea anemone and clownfish is one of the best examples of commensalism in nature.
OR
(b) Correctly depict (also indicate the trophic level) and describe the ecological pyramid of biomass in sea with 40 standing crop of phytoplankton supporting 90 standing crop of zooplankton which further supports 120 small fishes.

key_points: (a) Clownfish lives among the tentacles of sea anemone and gets protection; sea anemone is neither benefited nor harmed — this is commensalism.
(b) Inverted pyramid: Phytoplankton (T1, 40) → Zooplankton (T2, 90) → Small fish (T3, 120); biomass increases at higher trophic levels — inverted pyramid of biomass.

questions.solution:
(a) The interaction between sea anemone and clownfish is a classic example of commensalism. The clownfish lives among the stinging tentacles of the sea anemone and uses it as shelter, gaining protection from predators. The clownfish is benefited because it gets a safe habitat. The sea anemone, however, is neither significantly benefited nor harmed by the presence of the clownfish. Since only one partner (clownfish) benefits and the other (sea anemone) is unaffected, this is commensalism.

(b) Food chain: Phytoplankton (T1, 40) → Zooplankton (T2, 90) → Small fishes (T3, 120). The ecological pyramid of biomass in the sea is an inverted pyramid. Phytoplankton at T1 have the lowest standing biomass (40), zooplankton at T2 have 90, and small fishes at T3 have the highest biomass (120). This inverted pattern occurs because phytoplankton have a very rapid turnover rate — they reproduce quickly and are consumed quickly, so their standing crop at any moment is lower than the consumers they support.

(b) Translation starting from the second nucleotide (Reading frame 2): 5'-GUGGCACUCAGUCCUUAAUGGCG-3'

questions.solution: In case (a), the mRNA sequence 5'-CUCGCUUGCCGAUCAAGGGUUA-3' has 22 nucleotides. Reading in triplets from the first nucleotide: CUC-GCU-UGC-CGA-UCA-AGG-GUU and 'A' is left over (1 nucleotide). So 7 complete codons are formed, specifying 7 amino acids. In case (b), the mRNA sequence 5'-GUGGCACUCAGUCCUUAAUGGCG-3' has 23 nucleotides. Reading in triplets from the first nucleotide (which is the second nucleotide of frame 1): GUG-GCA-CUC-AGU-CCU-UAA-UGG and 'CG' remains. UAA is a stop codon, so translation stops there, giving only 6 amino acids (the stop codon does not code for an amino acid). Therefore, case (a) gives 7 amino acids and case (b) gives 6 amino acids (since UAA is a stop codon).

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain how the immunity of a person is affected if there is atrophy (degeneration) of the thymus gland at an early stage of life.
OR
(b) (i) What are interferons? Explain their role in providing immunity to a person. (ii) Which category of innate immunity defence barrier can interferons be classified into?

key_points: (a) Thymus is site of T-lymphocyte maturation; its atrophy leads to deficiency of T-cells, severely weakening cell-mediated immunity.
(b)(i) Interferons are glycoproteins secreted by virus-infected cells that protect neighbouring cells from viral infection.
(b)(ii) Interferons are classified under physiological barriers of innate immunity.

questions.solution:
(a) The thymus gland is the primary lymphoid organ where T-lymphocytes (T-cells) mature and become immunocompetent. If the thymus undergoes atrophy (degeneration) at an early stage of life, T-cell maturation will be severely impaired. This leads to a drastic reduction in the number of functional T-cells, causing a significant weakening of cell-mediated immunity. The person becomes highly susceptible to intracellular pathogens, viruses, and certain cancers. Humoral immunity (antibody production by B-cells) is also reduced because many B-cell responses require T-helper cell assistance.

(b)(i) Interferons are small glycoprotein molecules secreted by virus-infected cells. When a cell is infected by a virus, it secretes interferons which bind to receptors on neighbouring uninfected cells and stimulate them to produce antiviral proteins. These antiviral proteins prevent viral replication inside those cells, thereby protecting them from infection. Interferons thus provide non-specific protection and help slow the spread of viral infection. (ii) Interferons can be classified under the physiological barriers of innate immunity.

questions.text_english:
(a) Write two features of an ideal contraceptive. Explain any one natural contraceptive method that makes the chances of conception almost nil.
OR
(b) Explain GIFT and ICSI.

key_points: (a) Ideal contraceptive: user-friendly, easily available, no/minimal side effects, reversible; Lactational amenorrhoea — absence of menstruation during intense lactation after parturition.
(b) GIFT: transfer of ovum from donor to fallopian tube of recipient. ICSI: direct injection of sperm into egg in laboratory.

questions.solution:
(a) Two features of an ideal contraceptive are: (1) it should be user-friendly and easily available, causing minimal side effects on the user's health; and (2) it should be reversible and have no long-term adverse effects on reproductive capacity. One natural contraceptive method that makes the chances of conception almost nil is Lactational Amenorrhoea. During intense lactation immediately following parturition (childbirth), the high levels of prolactin hormone suppress ovulation and menstruation. Since no ovulation occurs, there is no egg to be fertilised, making conception highly unlikely during this period. It is fully effective only up to six months after delivery.

(b) GIFT (Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer): In this procedure, an ovum collected from a donor female is transferred into the fallopian tube of a recipient female who cannot produce eggs but can support a pregnancy. The egg is fertilised naturally within the fallopian tube. ICSI (Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection): In this technique, a single sperm is directly injected into the cytoplasm of a mature egg (ovum) in the laboratory to achieve fertilisation, especially when the male partner has very low sperm count or motility.

questions.text_english: Explain the biological treatment of primary effluent when passed into the large aeration tanks in a sewage treatment plant (STP).

key_points: Secondary treatment: aerobic microorganisms decompose organic matter in primary effluent
Formation of flocs (masses of bacteria with fungal filaments)
BOD is significantly reduced; effluent is then passed to settling tank

questions.solution: When primary effluent (the liquid obtained after removal of large solids) is passed into large aeration tanks, secondary treatment (biological treatment) takes place. In the aeration tanks, the effluent is vigorously agitated and aerated by mechanical stirrers. This promotes the growth of useful aerobic heterotrophic microorganisms, mainly bacteria. These bacteria decompose and consume the dissolved organic matter present in the primary effluent, significantly reducing its Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD). During this process, the bacteria aggregate to form masses called flocs — these are masses of bacteria held together by a network of fungal filaments, forming mesh-like structures. Once the BOD of the effluent is reduced substantially, it is transferred to a settling tank (secondary settling tank) where the flocs settle down as activated sludge. The clear supernatant (secondary effluent) with greatly reduced BOD is then released or treated further.

questions.text_english:
Thomas Hunt Morgan carried out several dihybrid crosses in Drosophila melanogaster to study genes that were sex linked.
(a) Give four major reasons for using the tiny fruit flies by Morgan for his experiments.
(b) How did Morgan and his group explain the physical association of the two genes on a chromosome to the frequency of recombination between gene pairs on the same chromosome?

key_points: (a) Short life cycle, large number of offspring, easy and inexpensive to maintain, many heritable morphological characters, only 4 pairs of chromosomes.

(b) Genes located close together on the same chromosome are tightly linked and recombine less frequently; genes located farther apart recombine more frequently — recombination frequency is proportional to physical distance.

questions.solution:
(a) The four major reasons why Morgan chose Drosophila melanogaster for his experiments are: (1) Drosophila has a very short life cycle of about two weeks, allowing many generations to be studied quickly; (2) a single mating produces a very large number of offspring (hundreds), providing statistically significant data; (3) the fruit flies are very easy and cheap to maintain in the laboratory on simple growth media; and (4) Drosophila has only four pairs of chromosomes, making genetic analysis simpler, and also exhibits many clearly distinguishable heritable morphological characteristics.

(b) Morgan and his group proposed the concept of linkage to explain their results. They found that when two genes are located on the same chromosome (linked genes), they tend to be inherited together rather than showing independent assortment. The frequency of recombination (cross-over) between two linked gene pairs was found to be proportional to the physical distance between them on the chromosome. Genes that are very close together on the same chromosome show very low recombination frequency (tight linkage), while genes that are far apart show higher recombination frequency. This led to the development of genetic maps where distances between genes are measured in map units (centiMorgans, cM).

questions.text_english: Explain the process of formation of placenta in a human female after the implantation of the blastocyst in the endometrium of the uterus.

key_points: After implantation, trophoblast cells proliferate and form finger-like projections called chorionic villi.
Chorionic villi interdigitate with uterine tissue (endometrium) to form the placenta.
Placenta functions as the interface for nutrient, gas, and waste exchange between mother and foetus.

questions.solution: After the blastocyst implants into the endometrium of the uterus, the outer trophoblast layer of the blastocyst proliferates and its cells begin to differentiate. The trophoblast cells invade the endometrial tissue and develop finger-like projections called chorionic villi. These chorionic villi grow and interdigitate deeply with the uterine endometrial tissue. The maternal blood spaces (sinusoids) surround the chorionic villi, bringing the maternal blood into close proximity with the foetal blood (though the two bloods do not directly mix). The chorionic villi and the corresponding uterine tissue together form the disc-shaped placenta. The placenta is connected to the developing embryo by the umbilical cord. It serves as the structural and functional unit for exchange of nutrients (glucose, amino acids), oxygen, and waste products (CO2, urea) between the mother and the foetus throughout the gestational period.

questions.text_english:
According to a recent wildlife report, the biggest threat to the tiger's survival in Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR) was found to be a small, beautiful flower, Lantana camara, a tropical American shrub, that invaded 40% of India's tiger range. Tamil Nadu department's Lantana weed eradication drive helped to restore the dying MTR thereby also reducing human-wildlife conflicts. MTR is home to 25 species of grasses and legumes.
(a) Explain how did the removal of Lantana help in restoring the dying Mudumalai Tiger Reserve.
(b) Why is the invasion of Lantana camara a cause of concern in MTR?

key_points: (a) Removal of Lantana allowed native grasses and legumes to regenerate, providing natural habitat and food for herbivores which are prey for tigers.
(b) Lantana is an invasive alien species that competes with and displaces native vegetation (25 grass/legume species), reduces biodiversity, and disrupts the food chain.

questions.solution:
(a) Lantana camara is an invasive alien species that had overtaken large areas of MTR, forming dense thickets and suppressing the growth of native grasses and legumes. By eradicating Lantana, the native vegetation (grasses and legumes) was able to regenerate and recover. This restored the natural grassland habitat which supports populations of herbivores such as deer and other prey animals. A healthy prey base in turn supports tiger populations. Additionally, the restoration reduced areas where tigers and humans might come into conflict at the forest edges, thereby reducing human-wildlife conflict as well.

(b) Lantana camara is an invasive alien species originally from tropical America. Its rapid and aggressive spread has invaded 40% of India's tiger range. It forms dense monocultures that outcompete and displace the 25 native species of grasses and legumes that form the natural vegetation of MTR. This loss of native plant diversity reduces the food available for herbivores, which in turn reduces the prey base for tigers. The dense Lantana thickets also alter the microhabitat, reduce water availability, and make it difficult for wildlife to move freely. All these factors threaten the survival of tigers and biodiversity of MTR.

(i) Which one of the two — lampreys' or macaques' evolution is more closely related to humans and why?
OR
(ii) Which one of the two — frogs' or dogs' evolution is more closely related to humans and why?

key_points: (i) Macaque is more closely related to humans — only 8 amino acid differences vs 125 for lamprey.
(ii) Dog is more closely related to humans — only 32 amino acid differences vs 67 for frog.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) Macaque evolution is more closely related to humans. The haemoglobin of macaques differs from human haemoglobin by only 8 amino acids, whereas lamprey haemoglobin differs by 125 amino acids. Fewer amino acid differences indicate greater biochemical similarity and therefore a more recent common ancestor and closer evolutionary relationship. Both humans and macaques are primates and share a much more recent common ancestor compared to the ancient common vertebrate ancestor shared with lampreys.

(ii) Dogs (canines) are more closely related to humans in an evolutionary sense compared to frogs. The haemoglobin of dogs differs from human haemoglobin by only 32 amino acids, while frog haemoglobin differs by 67 amino acids. Fewer amino acid differences indicate a more recent common ancestor and closer evolutionary relationship. Dogs are mammals (class Mammalia), sharing the same class as humans, while frogs are amphibians (class Amphibia), representing an earlier divergence from the common vertebrate ancestor.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Describe the population growth curve applicable in a population of any species in nature that has limited resources at its disposal. (ii) Give the equation of this growth curve. (iii) Name the growth curve and depict a graphical plot for this type of population growth.
OR
(b) (i) Explain the Species-Area relationship within a natural forest and also predict the nature of graph when species richness is plotted against the area for a wide variety of taxa. (ii) Depict the graphical relationship between species richness and area. (iii) Give the equation of the Species-Area relationship for a wide variety of taxa on a logarithmic scale.

key_points: (a)(i) Logistic growth: population grows slowly at first, then rapidly, then slows and plateaus at K (carrying capacity).
(a)(ii) dN/dt = rN[(K-N)/K]
(a)(iii) S-shaped (Sigmoid / Logistic) curve with time on X-axis and population size (N) on Y-axis.
(b)(i) As area increases, species richness increases; for large areas the graph is a straight line on a log scale.
(b)(ii) Species richness vs area gives a rectangular hyperbola (or straight line on log-log scale).
(b)(iii) log S = log C + Z log A

questions.solution:
(a) When resources are limited, a population in nature shows logistic growth. Initially, when population size is small and resources are abundant relative to the number of individuals, the population grows slowly (lag phase). Then as conditions improve, growth accelerates (exponential phase). However, as population size approaches the carrying capacity (K) of the environment — the maximum number of individuals the environment can sustain — growth begins to slow down due to increasing competition for limited resources, predation, disease, and other factors. Finally, the population stabilises around K, resulting in a characteristic S-shaped (sigmoid) curve.

The equation for logistic growth is: dN/dt = rN[(K - N)/K], where N = population size, r = intrinsic rate of natural increase, K = carrying capacity, and (K - N)/K is the fraction of resources still available. This curve is called the Logistic Growth Curve or S-shaped Sigmoid Curve. On a graph, time is plotted on the X-axis and population size (N) on the Y-axis; the curve rises slowly, then steeply, then levels off at K.

(b) The Species-Area relationship states that within a natural forest or region, as the area (A) increases, the number of species (species richness, S) also increases. When species richness is plotted against area on a normal (arithmetic) scale, the relationship produces a rectangular hyperbola. However, for a wide variety of taxa (insects, plants, birds, etc.) when plotted on a log-log scale (log S vs log A), the relationship becomes a straight line. The equation on a logarithmic scale is: log S = log C + Z log A, where S = species richness, A = area, Z = slope of the line (regression coefficient, typically between 0.1 and 0.2 for small islands/regions and about 0.6 for large continental areas), and C = Y-intercept (a constant related to the type of organism and region).

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Explain how does double fertilisation take place in a flowering plant. (ii) Write the fate of the products of double fertilization in these plants.
OR
(b) (i) Explain the structure of testicular lobules in human male reproductive system. Name the two types of cells present in the seminiferous tubules and state their role. (ii) Describe the role of hypothalamic hormone GnRH in spermatogenesis.

key_points: (a)(i) Pollen tube releases two male gametes; one fuses with egg (syngamy → zygote); other fuses with secondary nucleus (triple fusion → PEN/endosperm nucleus).
(a)(ii) Zygote → embryo; PEN → triploid endosperm; ovule → seed; ovary → fruit.
(b)(i) Each testis has 250 testicular lobules, each containing 1-3 seminiferous tubules; Sertoli cells (nourish sperm) and spermatogonia (produce sperm).
(b)(ii) GnRH stimulates anterior pituitary to release LH and FSH; LH acts on Leydig cells to produce testosterone; FSH acts on Sertoli cells to support spermatogenesis.

questions.solution:
(a)(i) In a flowering plant, the pollen grain germinates on the stigma and the pollen tube grows through the style, eventually entering the ovule through the micropyle. The pollen tube carries two male gametes (sperm cells). Upon entering the embryo sac, it releases both sperm cells. One male gamete fuses with the egg cell (the female gamete) in a process called syngamy or generative fertilisation, forming the diploid zygote (2n). Simultaneously, the second male gamete fuses with the secondary nucleus (formed by fusion of the two polar nuclei) in a process called triple fusion or vegetative fertilisation, forming the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) (3n). Since fertilisation occurs twice, this is called double fertilisation, a unique feature of angiosperms. (ii) The zygote (2n) undergoes repeated mitotic divisions to develop into the embryo. The primary endosperm nucleus (3n) divides to form the triploid endosperm, which serves as the nutritive tissue for the developing embryo. The ovule develops into the seed, while the ovary wall develops into the fruit wall (pericarp), and the entire ovary develops into the fruit.

(b)(i) Each testis is divided into about 250 compartments called testicular lobules by septa of connective tissue. Each lobule contains one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules, where spermatogenesis takes place. The two types of cells present in the seminiferous tubules are: Sertoli cells (sustentacular cells) — these are large supporting cells that provide nourishment to the developing sperm cells (spermatids), produce inhibin, and create the blood-testis barrier; and Spermatogonia (male germ cells) — these are the precursor cells that undergo mitosis and meiosis to produce spermatozoa. Outside the seminiferous tubules, interstitial spaces contain Leydig cells which produce the male sex hormone testosterone. (ii) Spermatogenesis begins at puberty under the influence of Gonadotropin Releasing Hormone (GnRH) secreted by the hypothalamus. GnRH acts on the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland, stimulating it to secrete two gonadotropins: Luteinising Hormone (LH) and Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH). LH acts on the Leydig cells in the interstitial tissue of the testis, stimulating them to produce and secrete testosterone. Testosterone, in turn, stimulates the process of spermatogenesis. FSH acts on the Sertoli cells, stimulating them to secrete factors that support spermatogenesis and the maturation of spermatids into spermatozoa.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Name the two genes encoding for the Bt toxin protein used in biotechnology for the control of cotton bollworms. (ii) How does the expression of Bt toxin gene in Bt cotton plant help in providing resistance to cotton bollworms? Explain.
OR
(b) (i) Explain the given methods of introducing the alien DNA in the host cells: (I) Biolistics (II) Microinjection. (ii) How is E. coli made 'competent' to take up a recombinant plasmid or DNA?

key_points: (a)(i) cry IAc and cry IIAb
(a)(ii) Bt toxin is produced as inactive protoxin; alkaline gut of bollworm activates it; toxin binds to midgut epithelium causing pores, cell swelling and death.
(b)(i) Biolistics: DNA-coated gold/tungsten particles fired into cells using gene gun. Microinjection: DNA directly injected into nucleus using micropipette.
(b)(ii) E. coli treated with divalent cations (Ca2+) on ice, then heat shock — pores form in cell membrane allowing DNA uptake.

questions.solution:
(a)(i) The two genes encoding Bt toxin proteins used to control cotton bollworms are cry IAc (which encodes a protein effective against cotton bollworm Helicoverpa armigera) and cry IIAb (also effective against bollworms). These genes are derived from the soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis.

(a)(ii) In Bt cotton plants, the cry gene (such as cry IAc) is incorporated into the plant genome and expressed in the plant cells. The Bt toxin (Cry protein) is produced in the plant as an inactive protoxin. When the cotton bollworm larva feeds on the Bt cotton plant, it ingests this protoxin. The highly alkaline environment (high pH) in the midgut of the insect activates the inactive protoxin, converting it into the active toxic form. The activated toxin then binds to specific receptor proteins on the epithelial cell surfaces of the midgut of the insect. This binding creates pores in the cell membrane, leading to cell swelling and lysis. The midgut epithelial cells are destroyed, the insect stops feeding and eventually dies. Since the receptor for the Bt toxin is specific to certain insects, the toxin does not harm other organisms including humans.

(b)(i) Biolistics (Gene Gun method): In this method, microscopic particles of gold or tungsten are coated with the desired DNA (alien DNA) to be introduced into the host cell. These DNA-coated particles are then bombarded (fired) at high velocity into the target plant cells or tissues using a device called the gene gun (particle gun or biolistics gun). The high-speed particles penetrate the cell wall and membrane and deliver the DNA directly into the nucleus of the cell, where it can integrate into the chromosomal DNA. This method is particularly useful for introducing DNA into plant cells which have rigid cell walls.

Microinjection: In this technique, the desired recombinant DNA is directly injected into the nucleus of the host cell using a very fine glass micropipette (microneedle) under a microscope with a micromanipulator. This is a highly precise method used particularly for animal cells, embryonic cells, or cells that are difficult to transform by other methods.

(b)(ii) E. coli cells do not naturally take up foreign DNA from the environment. To make E. coli competent (able to take up recombinant plasmid or foreign DNA), the bacteria are first treated with divalent cations such as calcium chloride (CaCl2) solution while being kept on ice. The Ca2+ ions weaken the negatively charged bacterial cell membrane (by neutralising the negative charges), making it more permeable. The recombinant DNA is then added and the mixture is briefly subjected to a heat shock — it is rapidly shifted to 42°C for a short period and then immediately returned to ice. This heat shock treatment causes transient pores to form in the cell membrane, allowing the DNA to enter the cell. The competent cells thus prepared can incorporate the foreign plasmid DNA.
